thread.title_full: Resumption of Family Detention Under Trump Administration

author: VALERIE GONZALEZ
title: Resumption of Family Detention Under Trump Administration
text:
• The Trump administration resumed family detention of immigrants in South Texas after a pause during the Biden administration.
• Fourteen immigrant families with children as young as 1 year old are currently detained at a facility in Karnes County, Texas.
• The families originate from Colombia, Romania, Iran, Angola, Russia, Armenia, Turkey, and Brazil.
• Some families had been in the U.S. for as little as 20 days, while others had been there for about 10 years.
• The nonprofit RAICES provides services to families at the detention center.
• The Karnes County Immigration Processing Center is operated by Geo Group and has a capacity of 1,328 people.
• Geo Group's contract with the federal government runs through August 2029 and is expected to generate about $79 million in revenue in its first year.
• CoreCivic announced a contract with ICE to hold immigrant families at the South Texas Family Residential Center in Dilley, Texas, which has a capacity of 2,400 people.
• Immigration advocates have raised concerns about the welfare of children in detention.
• Dr. Alan Shapiro, a cofounder of Terra Firma National, reported behavioral regression and mental health issues among detained children during previous administrations.
